Exercise D.7 — Small gain versus the circle criterion
      
      
        Close the loop of Exercise D.6 as $w=-\phi(z)$ with $\phi(v)=\kappa\tanh v$, $\kappa\gt0$. (a) Which $\kappa$ does the small-gain theorem certify? (b) Which does the circle criterion certify ($\phi$ in the sector $[0,\kappa]$)? (c) Compare with the constant gains $\phi(v)=kv$.
        
          Show answer
          
            (a) The gain of $\kappa\tanh$ is $\kappa$ (slope at most $\kappa$), that of $H$ is $3$: small gain needs $3\kappa\lt1$, i.e. $\kappa\lt\tfrac13$.
            (b) $\mathrm{Re}\,H(e^{j\omega})=\frac{0.6(\cos\omega-0.8)}{1.64-1.6\cos\omega}$ is increasing in $\cos\omega$ (its derivative in $\cos\omega$ is $0.6\cdot0.36/(1.64-1.6\cos\omega)^2\gt0$), so its minimum is at $\omega=\pi$: $0.6(-1.8)/3.24=-\tfrac13$. The circle condition $1+\kappa\,\mathrm{Re}\,H\ge\varepsilon\gt0$ holds for all $\omega$ iff $\kappa\lt3$.
            (c) $x_{t+1}=(0.8-0.6k)x_t$ is stable iff $-\tfrac13\lt k\lt3$. The circle criterion recovers the whole constant-gain range $[0,3)$ for every nonlinearity in the sector (first-order loop), whereas small gain, which ignores the sign of the feedback, gives only a ninth of it.

reviewed_clauses.per_clause_reason: Actual complex exponential unit-circle bridge, reverse triangle denominator bound and omega0 attainer prove IsGreatest and the true sSup3, directly matching the source transfer from D6.
hypotheses: Exact source scalar discrete plant xnext=(4/5)x+w,z=(3/5)x,negative feedback w=-phi(z),source kappa>0. Formal results valid also for kappa=0 are harmless extensions; no positivity hypothesis is omitted.

H infinity is the actual supremum of the complex transfer modulus over the unit circle; the source nonlinearity gain is the least global origin gain and has the genuine incremental Lipschitz upper bound. Small-gain certification means its literal strict product test; direct source-trajectory convergence and epsilon/delta stability are independently derived.

The source product sector phi(z)*(phi(z)-kappa*z)<=0 is genuinely equivalent to phi0=0 and the radial inequalities for EVERY nonnegative kappa, including zero. Actual time-varying product-sector trajectories are recursively constructed and their all-initial geometric decay and epsilon/delta stability derived, with no existence or stability conclusion supplied as a premise.

Stable in the constant linear-gain answer means Schur/asymptotic stability as in the nearby Schur and absolute-stability definitions. The actual theorem proves both Lyapunov stability and all-initial attraction on the open interval; it does not falsely claim boundary gains are Lyapunov unstable.

The comparison one ninth is the exact ratio of the positive upper certification thresholds (1/3)/3. The larger negative-gain interval is explicitly stated separately; no measure-of-an-unbounded-parameter-space assertion is intended.

material_units.source_text: (b) $\mathrm{Re}\,H(e^{j\omega})=\frac{0.6(\cos\omega-0.8)}{1.64-1.6\cos\omega}$ is increasing in $\cos\omega$ (its derivative in $\cos\omega$ is $0.6\cdot0.36/(1.64-1.6\cos\omega)^2\gt0$), so its minimum is at $\omega=\pi$: $0.6(-1.8)/3.24=-\tfrac13$. The circle condition $1+\kappa\,\mathrm{Re}\,H\ge\varepsilon\gt0$ holds for all $\omega$ iff $\kappa\lt3$.

material_units.source_text: (c) $x_{t+1}=(0.8-0.6k)x_t$ is stable iff $-\tfrac13\lt k\lt3$. The circle criterion recovers the whole constant-gain range $[0,3)$ for every nonlinearity in the sector (first-order loop), whereas small gain, which ignores the sign of the feedback, gives only a ninth of it.
